newsitem.title: USA: Maine Yankee says no restart date for power plant.
newsitem.headline: Maine Yankee says no restart date for power plant.

text.p: Maine Yankee said Monday further corrective action and public hearings required before restarting the 910 megawatt Maine Yankee nuclear power plant have led the company to drop any target restart date.

"Maine Yankee's Readiness Plan notes that a mid-July restart is possible under the current work schedule but that additional items must be addressed. Therefore, no specific restart date is targeted at this time," the company said.
The company, in a statement, said eight key projects will need to be tackled before the nuclear plant can seek regulatory approval to return to service.

The eight projects include circuitry testing, electrical cable separation review, off-site power, steam generator inspection, fuel replacement, corrective action program, surveillance testing and cable submergence issues.
Following completion of these projects, Maine Yankee said it will need to review the corrective action program and maintenance backlogs to see if all requirements have been met.
In addition, there will be assessments of plant safety systems, major departments and key programs prior to restart.
"This will be the most comprehensive review the plant has ever undertaken, and we full expect to find areas to improve," Maine Yankee President Mike Sellman said.

Maine Yankee's Restart Readiness Plan will then be reviewed by the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) in a public meeting, followed by a Restart Plan Closure Report, which will be required 30-60 days prior to restart.
The public will be given a second chance to comment on the plant's restart.
The Maine Yankee unit is located in Wiscasset, Maine.

Maine Yankee is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, seven percent by Bangor Hydro-Electric Co, five percent by Maine Public Service Co, and 10 percent by other New England utilities.
